name: Fortebraccio Pikemen
headerMeta: Heroic era · Pike/Polearm infantry · anti-cav · 235 leadership

origin.text: Seasonal unit from the Heroic Era.

pitch: A strong anti-cavalry pike line that thrives in open fields when played in dispersed F1 formation. Requires careful positioning and a bug-workaround on brace commands to prevent cavalry from walking through.

doctrines.name: Anti-Cavalry Doctrine
doctrines.effect: -30% to -35% DMG taken from cavalry while bracing (tier varies by card copy).
doctrines.note: −40% cavalry damage taken while bracing, +16% damage vs. cavalry while bracing {1}; or lower tier (−30% cavalry damage) if needed for other slots {1}

doctrines.name: Epic Polearm Doctrine (Pike Charge)
doctrines.effect: Pike Charge doctrine: unlocks a charge order that can one-shot diving heroes; allows a 180 degree turn to re-brace if flanked.
doctrines.note: Counters diving heroes and re-braces after impact {1,2}

doctrines.name: Epic Bloodthirsty Doctrine
doctrines.effect: 12% lifesteal for 6s after dealing damage, +12% DMG when HP above 60%.
doctrines.note: Lifesteal + 12% damage; swap in if sustain is a priority over raw output {1}

doctrines.name: Epic Leadership Doctrine
doctrines.note: Substitute for Pike Charge if you prefer flat regroup benefits {1}

doctrines.name: Stun / Static Doctrines
doctrines.note: The unit already has sufficient cavalry damage; widespread crowd-control immunity makes these underperform {2}

battleRole.positioning: Place in F1 super-dispersed formation in open areas to maximize anti-cavalry coverage without allowing a single hero disruption to unbrace the whole unit {2}. In siege or street maps with tight corridors, F2 line formation works {1,2}, but avoid stacking — keep units spread forward and back to limit how many can be hit and unbraced by a breakthrough {2}.
battleRole.formation: F1 super-dispersed (open field) or F2 line staggered (siege) — never tight block formation {1,2}
battleRole.tips: The instant-brace command has a known bug: always press V (ready) before brace to mitigate it — without V, the unit often continues moving to its last-ordered location instead of bracing, letting cavalry walk through {2}. Use the follow-the-front-line routine: gather formation, advance (X), follow (F), press V, then brace — repeat every reposition {2}. Staggered spacing allows front rows to act as a wall absorbing charges while rear rows stay braced and functional {2}. Use long-range positioning behind Spartans or phalanx formations to add anti-cavalry protection while dealing heavy front-line damage {1}.

cards.name: Condottieri Guard / unsupported cavalry charges
cards.why: One of the strongest braces in the game — an unsupported charge gets wiped almost instantly, but even minimal CC support from one melee hero flips it and pikes that lose formation fall apart fast {3}

cards.name: Crowd-control heroes
cards.why: Any hero that jumps on a tight formation breaks brace for the whole unit; tight block formation is a hard weakness {2}

cards.name: Sipahis with Croupade
cards.why: Croupade's burst-speed gimmick is wasted — Fortebraccio doesn't need speed to hit hard, so the tempo swing does nothing for you {4}

matchups.pressure: You pressure: Heavy anti-cavalry front-line support for slow-moving units (Spartans, phalanx formations) while being immobile yourself {1}

controls.notes: Repositioning sequence (gather formation → advance (X) → follow (F) → ready (V) → brace → hold) {2}. Deliberately avoid Stun or anti-cavalry-damage doctrines in favor of flat damage that boosts minimum output vs. both unit types {2}.
